metadata.creator: Upham, Alfred H.
metadata.description: Alfred H. Upham, president of Miami University, writes to Murray Sheehan regarding the admission of an unnamed prospective student to Miami University as a freshman. The letter notes the good records of other boys from Thailand, refers to a university in Bangkok and its entrance examinations, and says that a room can be held while the university tries to place the student in a freshman dormitory.
metadata.title: Letter to Mr. Murray Sheehan regarding admission, 8 September 1941
metadata.transcript:
[page 1]
September 8, 1941

Mr. [Mister] Murray Sheehan
Worcester 59
Gloucester, Massachusetts

Dear Murray:

Replying to your letter of September 6, I can assure you that we shall be pleased to admit [illegible] [illegible] to Miami University as a freshman.

While of course we know nothing of the University you mention in Bangkok or of its entrance examinations, the other boys from Thailand have made such a good record here that we do not hesitate.

Freshman Week begins with a convocation next Sunday evening, September 14, but we can hold a room for him a little longer if necessary. We are trying to squeeze him into one of the freshman dormitories.

Cordially yours,

President

[handwritten] [illegible]
